verification.notes: Hall later stated publicly that All Things Possible Ministries funded five FoldAR systems for a local school and that after summer 2024 the ministry made no further school-resource-officer effort. This is a firsthand account and is consistent with the publicly promoted school mission, though no independent invoice was located.

records.text: Victor Marx says his headquarters holds more than 6,000 letters from incarcerated children with whom his organization corresponded and who were helped by its work.
records.speaker: Victor Marx

appearances.snippet: And probably the difference between me and maybe others that, you know, I've done stuff is there, we don't charge people to set them free. We do this out of love. There's no financial benefit for it, especially kids are incarcerated, but I have over 6,000 letters. ... Here in our headquarters of kids that we've written, we've corresponded back and forth that really were helped in this.

verification.notes: Current Christian Broadcasting Network reporting states that Marx and the ministry received about 6,000 letters from incarcerated children who were helped and encouraged. records.text: Victor Marx says the Kurdistan government officially invited his organization into Iraq to help people who had been held captive by the Islamic State.
records.speaker: Victor Marx

appearances.snippet: And the purpose was we had an invitation by the Kurdistan government. We had access placement and an official invitation to go in to help those who had been held captive by ISIS.

verification.notes: ATP activity in Iraq is independently documented, but no Kurdistan Regional Government invitation naming Marx or ATP was located. Current reporting says the Kurdish government did not respond to requests to verify his operational claims.

records.text: Victor Marx says All Things Possible Ministries has never accepted government funding.
records.speaker: Victor Marx

appearances.snippet: They were lacking what we provided dignity kits for personal hygiene. We provided food. We provided water. We started providing surgeries as our donations came in and never did we take. ... take any governmental funding. To this day, we have it.

verification.notes: ATP currently states that it receives no government funding. IRS Form 990 data for the ministry show revenue reported overwhelmingly or entirely as contributions across the available years and no identified government program revenue, supporting the claim, though the absolute word never cannot be independently audited beyond available filings.

records.text: Victor Marx says neither he nor All Things Possible Ministries ever claimed to have rescued 45,000 people; he says the organization helped that many and rescued some.
records.speaker: Victor Marx

appearances.snippet: What I'm saying is I've never, me said or written or our organization ever declared we rescued 45,000. We've helped. ... We've provided trauma relief and some we've definitely rescued because it's part of what we do. Our mission statement for all things possible ministries is to set captives free physically, emotionally and spiritually.

verification.notes: Current reporting documents that the official campaign website stated that Marx had rescued more than 45,000 women and children before the wording was removed. The site was an authorized campaign publication, directly contradicting the categorical claim that neither Marx nor his organizations ever published that rescue figure.

records.text: Victor Marx says his team rescued a mother who had been held captive by the Islamic State for nine years and had two children in captivity, after planning the mission for six months and executing it in five days.
records.speaker: Victor Marx

appearances.snippet: that was a rescue of a mom who had been held captive nine years. She was kidnapped as a teenager, had two children inside of captivity of ISIS, and we planned a mission for six months, executed in five days. ... It's documented, and she's back home with her family.

verification.notes: Marx has repeated a similar rescue account in other interviews, but current searches found no name, partner record, government record, or independent report establishing the nine-year captivity, two children, six-month planning period, or five-day execution.

records.text: Victor Marx says he has never intentionally manipulated or maligned anyone or pursued ministry relationships for money.
records.speaker: Victor Marx

appearances.snippet: Candace, I'm human. I've messed up plenty. But in the air of integrity? I've never intentionally gone after anybody. ... intentionally going after anybody I've never manipulated malign or or try to do things for money so yeah I mean watch my film read one of my two books I talk about plenty of self-evident you know ways that I depend on the grace of God

verification.notes: This is a categorical claim about intent across all relationships. Current sources contain serious competing allegations but no record capable of proving or disproving the absolute internal-intent claim.

records.text: Victor Marx says his organization helped 6,000 children affected by the war between Hamas and Israel.
records.speaker: Victor Marx

appearances.snippet: Well, let me tell you, we helped 6,000 children who had been affected by the war between Hamas and Israel.

verification.notes: Public reporting confirms ATP distributed trauma tools and aid to children in Israel and the region, and Marx repeated the 6,000 figure in another interview. No independent beneficiary list, audit, partner report, or government record substantiating the 6,000 total was located.
